title: Penalty-based pre-relaxation with growing radii
spec: Before SLSQP, run a cheap vectorised pre-relaxation: minimise sum over pairs of max(0, ri+rj-dij)^2 plus wall violations minus lambda*sum r with L-BFGS-B (analytic gradient via numpy) for lambda increasing through 3 stages (0.01, 0.03, 0.1). Use the result as SLSQP's start. This produces feasible-ish, well-spread starts and should reduce the number of wasted SLSQP iterations and poor local optima.

title: Symmetry-seeded starts
spec: For 20% of explore restarts, draw 13 random centres and radii in the half-square or triangle and mirror them through the centre point (x,y)->(1-x,1-y) to give 26 circles. Add a small noise sd 0.005 and run SLSQP. Many best-known packings for this problem have approximate symmetry, so this halves the search dimension for those starts.

title: Small-circle count prior via fixed-size-class radius bounds
spec: For explore restarts, give SLSQP radius bounds that force a size structure: draw a random count k in 4..8 of circles whose radius upper bound is 0.2 and let the others have an upper bound of 0.09. Choose the bounded circles at random. Use the bounds only in the first 60 iterations, then lift them to [0,0.5] for the rest of the run, using a second minimize call from the result. This steers the restarts toward mixed-size layouts like the best known packing.

title: Early abort of poor restarts with warm continuation
spec: Run every restart first for only 60 SLSQP iterations. Compute the current radii sum (after clip and fast repair). Only if it exceeds the 60th percentile of the previous first-stage results (or the first 10 restarts are collected) continue the same solution with 300 more iterations, starting from the result. Otherwise discard. This concentrates compute on promising basins.

title: Trust-region basin acceptance with noise annealing
spec: In refinement, perturb the best packing with centre noise sd s drawn log-uniformly from [0.002,0.03] on each iteration, but apply it only to circles within distance 0.25 of a randomly chosen point (a local patch). This makes the perturbation spatially local, so a good global structure survives. Accept only improvements. Use SLSQP warm start with radii x0.95.

title: Batch of parallel perturbations, pick best by cheap proxy
spec: In each refinement step, generate 4 perturbed children of the best, and run a 30-iteration SLSQP on each. Then run the full 200 iteration SLSQP only for the one with the highest unrepaired radius sum. This differs from screening of random starts because it filters local neighbours of a strong solution. Accept the result if better than the best after repair.

title: Grow-radius continuation from best
spec: In refinement, build a start from the best packing by multiplying radii by 0.7, adding centre noise sd 0.01 to a random 40% of circles, then running SLSQP with maxiter 200. This lets the optimiser re-expand the circles into a different contact graph. It replaces the perturbation move for 50% of refinement iterations.

title: Ring-based structured starts
spec: For 50% of explore starts, create initial centres as: 4 circles near the corners (0.12 from each), 12 circles on a ring of radius about 0.38 around the centre with random phase, 9 circles at the inner 3x3 pattern scaled to 0.5 and jittered with sd 0.03, and one extra at a random point. Use initial radii 0.08 for the corners and 0.1 for the rest. This reflects the structure of the best known packings, which have a few big inner circles and a ring of smaller boundary circles. The other 50% stay random.

title: Symmetry-seeded starts
spec: Generate starts that are symmetric under reflection about the diagonal or about the vertical axis: sample 13 points and mirror them. Add noise. Many good packings are near-symmetric.

title: Cheap high-iteration restarts through early abort
spec: Explore restarts run SLSQP for 40 iterations and measure the sum of radii of the unrepaired iterate. Continue to the full 200 iterations only if that sum is above the median of the previous 20 first-stage sums. Otherwise discard the run. The continuation uses the same x as the start. Note that earlier slots tried similar ideas with fixed thresholds, so use this relative median rule and keep the code short.

title: Symmetric-seeded starts
spec: For half of the fresh random starts, draw 13 random points with radii 0.05 and build the packing as point-symmetric about the square centre (the point p and the point 1-p), so n=26 gives 13 pairs. Add small noise sd 0.005 to break exact symmetry and run SLSQP as usual. Many good known packings are near-symmetric.

title: Hole-targeted relocation
spec: In the refinement phase, add a move: remove the smallest-radius circle (or a random one of the 3 smallest). Sample 2000 random points in the square and compute for each the free radius, min(distance to other circle surfaces, distance to walls). Place the circle at the point with the largest free radius, with radius 0.5 of that, and run the full SLSQP from there. Use this in 40% of refinement steps and the normal shake otherwise. Accept if better.

title: Grow-radius continuation from best
spec: In the refinement phase, with probability 0.3 build the start by taking the best packing, scaling all radii by 0.8, and adding centre noise sd 0.01. Then run SLSQP. Shrinking the radii gives the circles room to rearrange, and SLSQP regrows them into a possibly different contact graph. The other hops stay as they are.

title: Walls as variable bounds
spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. Remove the four wall blocks and the r>=0 block from cons, keeping only the pairwise distance constraints plus the 4n wall constraints c-r>=0 (these must stay as constraints because they couple c and r). Only the r>=0 block becomes a bound. Also add analytic gradient of the objective (-ones for radii, 0 for centres). This is a small, clean constraint reduction. Keep everything else, including the slot 9 schedule, unchanged.

title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping
spec: In the refinement phase keep a current packing and a best packing. Accept a hop result with probability exp((new_sum-cur_sum)/T), with T=0.002 decaying linearly to 0.0002 over the phase. Perturb the current packing, not the best. Always remember the best-ever packing and return it. This lets the search leave the local basin while staying close to good structures.

title: Hole-targeted relocation with free-space sampling
spec: In refinement, pick the smallest 1 to 2 circles in the best packing. Sample 2000 random points in the square and compute for each the clearance max(0, min over circles of (dist - r_j), wall distance). Move each chosen circle to the point with the biggest clearance among the samples, with radius equal to 0.5 times that clearance, then run SLSQP with the normal maxiter. Accept if the sum improves. This is a targeted move into the biggest hole, unlike random relocation.

title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping
spec: In the refinement phase, keep a current packing cur and a best packing. Propose a perturbed child from cur, solve it, then accept it if its radius sum is greater than cur's sum minus T*log(1/u) with u~U(0,1) and T=0.002, so worse moves are sometimes accepted. Update best whenever a child beats it. Every 15 failures, reset cur to best. Return best.

title: Exact repair by LP at fixed centres with active pairs
spec: Replace the greedy pairwise shrinking in _repair with an exact scaling. Compute the maximum feasible radii at the given centres by linprog (maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij and r_i <= wall distance). Then subtract 1e-11 and verify the result. If the packing is invalid, fall back to the old repair. Apply this only to final candidates and to the accept test in refinement, not to every restart.

title: Hex-lattice perturbed starts
spec: For 30% of explore restarts, build x0 from a hexagonal lattice with a random spacing in [0.18,0.22], a random rotation and offset, keep the 26 points closest to the centre of the square (add random points if fewer than 26 lie inside), jitter by sd 0.02, set radii to 0.05, and run SLSQP as usual. The rest of the restarts remain random.

title: Early-abort of poor restarts
spec: Run 40 SLSQP iterations first. If the sum of radii is below 97% of the best so far, abandon the restart. Otherwise continue to 300 iterations. This cuts wasted time.

title: Replicate incumbent slot 9 structure with final tight polish
spec: Keep the current train.py logic as is (30% random restarts, then perturbation of best). Reserve the last ~5% of the time budget: take the best packing (before repair), run SLSQP with maxiter 1000 and ftol=1e-15 from it with radii scaled by 0.999999, then repair, and keep it only if the repaired sum is larger than best. This tightens the active constraints and reduces the repair loss.

title: Perturb by rescaling a random sub-block of the layout
spec: In refinement, apply a random affine map to the centres inside a random half-plane. The map is a shear or scale of 1 ± 0.05 about the half-plane's centroid. Clip the centres to [0,1], scale the radii by 0.9, and run SLSQP. This moves collective rows of circles and may unjam structures that single-circle noise cannot.

title: Warm start with n+1 circles then delete the smallest
spec: For some of the explore restarts, solve for 27 circles with SLSQP (100 iterations). Delete the circle with the smallest radius and run SLSQP again on the remaining 26 for the full 200 iterations. This gives a different basin distribution, with fewer tiny circles stuck in gaps.

title: Grow-radius continuation from best
spec: In refinement, start SLSQP from the best centres with all radii set to 0.7*best radii. The smaller radii give slack so circles can slide past each other and rearrange. Add centre noise sd 0.003. Use this in 30% of refinement steps and keep the best-only acceptance rule.

title: Optimise in float-reduced variable space using pair-neighbour list refresh
spec: Rewrite the SLSQP calls in refinement to include only the pairs with centre distance < r_i + r_j + 0.15 for the warm-started packing. After solving, check all the pairs. If any is violated, re-run with the full constraint set. Warm-started packings are near-feasible, so this cuts the constraint count from 325 to about 80 and makes each hop about 3 times faster, giving more hops in the same time.

title: Random initial radii
spec: In explore restarts, replace the fixed INIT_RADIUS with radii drawn uniformly from [0.02, 0.12] per circle, and sort so the larger radii are assigned to the centres nearest the corners and edges. The rest of the pipeline is unchanged. This gives a diverse spread of sizes, since the best known packings have mixed radii.

title: Reduced neighbour-list constraints refreshed per stage
spec: In refinement runs only, restrict the SLSQP pair constraints to pairs whose centre distance in the start packing is under 0.35. Run SLSQP, then re-check all pairs. If any pair violates, rebuild the list with the full set and rerun 50 iterations. The saved time per call gives more hops in the same budget. Explore restarts keep the full constraints.

title: Basin hopping with Metropolis acceptance at temperature
spec: After the 30% restart phase, do basin hopping from a current packing with Metropolis acceptance: accept a candidate with sum s' if s' > s or with probability exp((s'-s)/T) where T=0.002, decreasing linearly to 0.0002 by the end. Track the global best separately and return it. This differs from slot 28's fixed window because it uses a decaying temperature.

title: Parallel-tempering style pool of two walkers
spec: After the 30% explore phase, keep two walkers: the best packing, and a second walker that accepts moves worse by up to 0.01 and reverts to the best every 15 steps without improvement. Alternate steps between them using the slot 9 perturbation. Return the best sum seen. This adds diversity without a large elite pool.

title: Two-stage radii objective: sum r then sum r with log barrier
spec: For explore restarts, first run 80 SLSQP iterations maximising sum(log(r+1e-3)). This favours uniform radii and gives a feasible, well-spread arrangement. Then switch to the true sum(r) objective for 200 iterations. The aim is to produce better-spread starting basins than the random start.

title: Metropolis with larger moves on stagnation
spec: In the refinement phase, count consecutive failures to improve the best. After 15 failures, replace the base packing for perturbation with the best of 3 fresh short restarts (60 iterations, then full run), and reset the counter. The global best stays stored for the return value. This gives restarts from new basins when the local search is stuck, without a fixed 30% explore split.

title: Remove-and-regrow a local region
spec: In the refinement phase, with probability 0.4 pick a random point p in the square and delete all circles within distance 0.2 of it (cap at 6 circles). Re-place those circles at random positions inside that disc with radius 0.02. Keep the other circles unchanged at their radii times 0.95, and run full SLSQP. Accept if the repaired sum improves.

title: Two-radius-class greedy shaking
spec: In the refinement phase, add a move that picks two circles i and j with different radii that are neighbours (touching), swaps their radii only (not the centres), shrinks both by 10%, and runs SLSQP. Use this in 30% of steps. It tests the change of size assignments without moving the centres, which the earlier centre-swap moves did not do.

title: Log-barrier second stage
spec: For explore restarts, run SLSQP on -sum(r) for 100 iterations. Then run a second SLSQP stage with maxiter 100 on -sum(r) - 1e-4 * sum(log(slack_pairs + 1e-6)) summed over the 60 smallest pair slacks, which spreads the contacts. Finish with a normal SLSQP stage on -sum(r) for the remaining 100 iterations. This gives different basins than the plain run.

title: Replicate slot 9 structure with fixed seed offset check
spec: Reconstruct the slot 9 design exactly: 30% of the time budget on random restarts (existing explore logic), then in the remaining time perturb the best packing (50%: relocate 2-3 random circles to uniform positions with radius INIT_RADIUS*0.5; 50%: centre noise sd 0.02, as in _solve_once start handling), run SLSQP, and accept only if the repaired sum is strictly larger. Change nothing else. The purpose is to replicate the incumbent so that the real gain can be measured.

title: Two-walker basin hopping with periodic reset
spec: After the 30% restart phase, keep two walkers: the best packing and the second best distinct packing from the explore phase. Alternate perturbing each walker using the existing perturbation. A walker is replaced only by its own improvements. Every 25 failed steps for a walker, reset it to a fresh explore result (random restart). Return the best overall.

title: Active-set LP polish of radii and centres (sequential LP)
spec: After the main loop, apply 20 steps of sequential linear programming with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs) on the best packing. Variables are dx, dy, dr per circle, with trust region 0.01 shrinking by 0.7 on failure. The linearised non-overlap constraints cover near pairs only, plus wall constraints. Maximise sum dr. Accept a step only if the repaired true sum improves. This is a different local solver from SLSQP and can finish convergence that SLSQP leaves behind.

title: Two-walker pool with periodic reset
spec: In refinement, keep two walkers, A (the global best) and B (a separate walker that starts from the second-best explore result). Alternate perturbation steps between them, each accepting only improvements for its own walker. Every 40 steps, if B is still below A by more than 0.005, reset B to a fresh random-restart result. This keeps diversity without the elite-pool slowdown seen in slot 10.

title: Perturbation by radius-class jitter
spec: In refinement, with probability 0.3 multiply the best packing radii by lognormal noise (sd 0.15) while keeping the centres, then shrink them as needed so they are feasible, using the repair. Use the result as the SLSQP start. This changes size assignments without moving the centres.

title: Remove-and-regrow whole region perturbation
spec: In refinement, choose a random disc of radius 0.2 in the square. Re-randomise the centres of all circles inside it, with small radii of 0.02. Keep the others fixed and run SLSQP with maxiter 200. Accept if the sum improves. This is a larger-scale structured move than the single-circle relocation.

title: Two-walker pool with periodic reset
spec: In the refinement phase, keep two walkers: the global best and a second walker that starts from the second-best random-restart result. Alternate perturbation steps between them. Each walker accepts only improvements. Every 40 steps with no global improvement, replace the weaker walker by the best result of a fresh random restart.

title: Seed from 5x5 grid plus one, perturbed
spec: For 30% of explore restarts, place 25 circles on a 5x5 grid with radius 0.1 (spacing 0.2), add one extra circle at a random grid gap (a corner of four cells), then add centre noise sd 0.03 and set radii 0.08. Run the normal SLSQP. Refinement is unchanged. This targets the structure of the known best 26-circle packings, which are near-grid with some distortion.

title: Late-stage greedy hill climb with growing time
spec: Split refinement into two parts. In the first 60% of the remaining time keep the current perturbation. In the last 40%, use only small centre noise with sd 0.002 on a random subset of 8 circles and maxiter 100. This restricts the late search to cheap local moves around the best packing.

title: Bolder: n=26 from a perturbed 5x5 grid plus one
spec: For 30% of explore restarts, start from a 5x5 grid of centres at spacing 0.2 offset 0.1 with radius 0.09, plus one extra circle placed at a random point with radius 0.02. Add centre noise sd 0.02 and run SLSQP at the standard iteration count. This seeds the square-grid-like family that the best known packings partly resemble. The remaining 70% of explore restarts stay random.

title: Batch of 3 perturbed children, take the best
spec: In each refinement step, generate 3 children of the best with independent perturbations (a mix of relocate and noise moves). Run SLSQP with 80 iterations on each, then continue to the full 200 iterations only from the child whose unrepaired radius sum is largest. Accept if the repaired sum is better than the best.

title: Radius-class jitter perturbation
spec: In refinement, with probability 0.3 start from the best packing and multiply each radius by exp(N(0, 0.15)). Keep the centres, add centre noise with sd 0.002, and scale radii by 0.8 so that the start is feasible. Then run the standard SLSQP. This changes the size distribution, while the centres move little.

title: Radius-class jitter perturbation
spec: In refinement, a new move: sort the circles by radius, take the 8 smallest, and move each by gaussian noise sd 0.05 (clipped to [0.02,0.98]) with its radius set to 0.5x. The large circles keep their centres and radii scaled by 0.95. Run SLSQP at 200 iterations. Use this in 30% of refinement steps, mixed with the incumbent moves.

title: Grid-perturbed initialization
spec: Replace the uniform random start with a jittered 5x5 grid plus one extra circle (26 points). Add Gaussian noise of sd 0.03 to the centres. Use a start radius of about 0.08. Structured starts are closer to good packings.

title: Batch of 3 children, keep best
spec: In each refinement step, create 3 perturbed children of the best packing, using the existing perturbation each time. Run SLSQP on each with maxiter 100. Continue the one with the best unrepaired radius sum for up to 200 more iterations, then repair it and compare with the best.
